subject: Science
central_question: How does light travel and interact with materials, objects, mirrors, and small openings to produce shadows, reflections, and images?
in_scope_units: 11.1 Sources of Light—natural and artificial sources, luminous and non-luminous objects, moonlight as reflected sunlight, and responsible use and disposal of LED lamps.
11.2 Does Light Travel in a Straight Line?—Activities 11.1 and 11.2 using aligned holes and straight or bent pipes to test rectilinear propagation of light.
11.3 Light through Transparent, Translucent, and Opaque Materials—Activity 11.3, prediction and observation, and classification by how much light passes through.
11.4 Shadow Formation—requirements for a visible shadow, darker, lighter and faint shadows, and Activity 11.4 on changes in shape, size and sharpness.
11.5 Reflection of Light—Activities 11.5 and 11.6 showing that a shiny surface or plane mirror changes the direction of light.
11.6 Images Formed in a Plane Mirror—Activities 11.7 and 11.8 on object and image, same size, erect image, inability to obtain the image on a screen, apparent position and lateral inversion.
11.7 Pinhole Camera—Activities 11.9 and 11.10 showing image formation through a tiny hole and an inverted image on a screen.
11.8 Making Some Useful Items—construction and working of a periscope and kaleidoscope using plane mirrors and repeated reflections.
In a Nutshell, Let Us Enhance Our Learning Questions 1–12, and exploratory projects on fireflies, coloured light, multiple mirrors and small mirrors.
banned_topics: Laws of reflection using angles of incidence and reflection.
Refraction, lenses and image formation by lenses.
Dispersion of white light and rainbow formation.
Detailed wave theory or diffraction calculations.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Moon is a luminous object because it shines at night.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Moon is non-luminous; it appears bright because it reflects sunlight.

known_pitfalls.claim: Light can be seen through a bent pipe because it follows the shape of the pipe.
known_pitfalls.correction: Activity 11.2 shows that a candle flame is visible through a straight pipe but not a bent pipe because light travels in straight lines.
Opaque objects form darker shadows, translucent objects form lighter shadows, and some transparent objects can form faint shadows.

known_pitfalls.claim: Changing the colour of an opaque object changes the colour of its shadow.
known_pitfalls.correction: Activity 11.4 shows that the colour of the opaque object does not change the colour of the shadow.

known_pitfalls.claim: A plane-mirror image can be captured on a screen.
known_pitfalls.correction: The image formed by a plane mirror cannot be obtained on a screen.

known_pitfalls.claim: A pinhole-camera image is laterally inverted but upright.
known_pitfalls.correction: A pinhole camera forms an upside-down, inverted image on a screen, whereas a plane-mirror image is erect and laterally inverted.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Activities 11.1 and 11.2 to reason from observation to the conclusion that light travels in a straight line.
Use NCERT Activity 11.3 and Let Us Enhance Our Learning Question 2 to classify materials by the amount of light transmitted.
Use NCERT Activity 11.4 and Questions 5–6 to explain how object position and number of light sources change a shadow.
Use NCERT Activities 11.5–11.8 and Questions 8 and 10 to establish reflection and the properties of a plane-mirror image.
Use NCERT Activities 11.9–11.10 and Question 7 to explain why a pinhole camera forms an inverted image.
Use NCERT Question 11 to apply reflection in the design of a periscope.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The section 'Let Us Enhance Our Learning' contains Questions 1–12, followed by four Exploratory Projects.
